descriptionChirho: Possessing wisdom, discernment, or practical skill — used substantively of 'wise men/people' and predicatively of individuals who are wise or act wisely. Covers singular, plural, and comparative forms across 20 NT occurrences (Mt 11:25; 23:34; Rom 1:14, 22; 16:19, 27; 1 Cor 1:19-20, 25-27; 3:10, 18-20; 6:5; Jas 3:13; Jude 1:25). Multilingual evidence is unified: Spanish 'sabio/sabios/más sabio' all derive from the same root; Hindi 'बुद्धिमान/बुद्धिमानों/अधिक बुद्धिमान' consistently denote wisdom; Arabic 'حَكيمٌ/حُكَماءُ/أَحْكَمُ' are standard singular, broken plural, and elative of the same root ح-ك-م; Korean '지혜로운/지혜롭다' share the same stem; Swahili 'mwenye hekima/wenye hekima/hekima zaidi' use the same noun 'hekima' throughout. The comparative 'wiser' (1 Cor 1:25) is a grammatical degree, not a separate lexical sense.
